item.title: Glenn Schumann accepts Florida State job, stay in Athens through playoffs
item.description: ATHENS, GA - OCTOBER 04: Defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann of the Georgia Bulldogs looks on prior to the college football game between the Kentucky Wildcats and the Georgia Bulldogs on October 04, 2025, at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Florida State has made official the worst-kept secret in coaching carousel news, announcing that Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann will be the next head coach of the Seminoles. Schumann spent the last three seasons (four including the current one) at the helm of the UGA defense after serving as co-coordinator with current Oregon head coach Dan Lanning. In that time the Red and Black have finished 1st, 7th, 2nd, and now 1st again in scoring defense. Schumann served as a graduate assistant under Kirby Smart and Nick Saban at Alabama before coming to Athens, and was among the staff Smart was most eager to bring with him.At the time some even referred to Schumann as Smart’s ““secret weapon.” That might be overstating things a bit, because Smart knows a thing or two about defenses himself and Schumann’s contributions in Tuscaloosa weren’t that secretive. They certainly aren’t now, as he’s helped develop the Bulldog defense into a perennial standout, and has grown into one of the game’s premier in-game coaches. Georgia’s second half defensive adjustments under Schumanns have been remarkable at times. Schu will stay in Athens through the playoffs while beginning work on his staff and recruiting for the Noles. That’s certainly not ideal, but announcing the move now was probably the best of the bad options for Kirby. It allows Georgia to get the news out and move on before the playoffs. My sense is also that Kirby has known this was coming for a few days, and is likely already well into his search for a replacement. Given that three of the four men who have held the DC job under him have become Power 2 head coaches (the other is Will Muschamp, who’d already been on that ride), the Bulldog job will draw interest from all corners of the country. Congrats to Coach Schumann on a well-earned promotion. Now let’s go swat some Yellow Jackwts. Go ‘Dawgs!!!

item.description: Nov 7, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks head coach Shane Beamer directs his team against the Texas A&M Aggies in the second half at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) COLUMBIA, S.C. — South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer raised eyebrows Saturday night with an unusual postgame message following the Gamecocks’ 34-6 loss to Georgia. At the time, the brief exchange seemed like an unexpected acknowledgment of a developing college football coaching rumor. However, less than 48 hours later, Beamer’s words suddenly carried considerably more significance. And what initially appeared to be an innocent conversation between former colleagues now looks remarkably well-timed. Beamer’s Saturday night message takes on new meaning Following Georgia’s victory at Williams-Brice Stadium, Beamer approached Bulldogs defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann during the customary postgame exchanges. The two coaches, who previously worked together at Georgia, shared a brief conversation. However, Beamer’s message went beyond congratulating his former colleague. “I hope that FSU thing works out if that’s what you want,” Beamer told Schumann. The exchange was captured in footage shared by FOX Carolina News and subsequently circulated across social media. At the time, Schumann had emerged as a leading candidate for Florida State’s vacant head coaching position. However, the Seminoles had not announced a hire, and questions remained about whether Schumann would ultimately leave Athens. Beamer’s comment therefore attracted attention because of its timing. Now, those questions have largely been answered. Florida State developments change the conversation On Monday, ESPN reported that Schumann had agreed to a five-year deal to become Florida State’s next head coach. The agreement is expected to allow Schumann to remain with Georgia through the remainder of its season, including the College Football Playoff. The development gives Beamer’s Saturday night comments an entirely different context. What sounded like speculation over the weekend now appears to have foreshadowed one of the most significant coaching moves of the week. However, there is an important distinction. Beamer’s remarks do not establish that he knew an agreement was imminent. Schumann’s name had already surfaced publicly in connection with the Florida State vacancy. Nevertheless, the timing remains notable. Less than two days after Beamer referenced the opportunity directly, reports emerged that Schumann had agreed to take the job. item.title: 49ers secure a key piece of their future before kickoff in Mexico City
item.description: The modern era of the San Francisco 49ers isn’t going anywhere. On Monday, NFL insider Jay Glazer reported that the 49ers and John Lynch agreed to terms on a new multi-year contract that would keep him as the team’s general manager and President of Football Operations for the foreseeable future. Glazer also reported that Lynch and 49ers team owner Jed York shook hands to agree on the deal on the sideline, before the team’s 35-10 victory against the Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday night. The San Francisco 49ers agree to a contract extension with John Lynch as general manager and President of Football Operations. AP Photo/Julio Cortez Lynch came into this season on an expiring deal and was considered to be on the hot seat, due to the team’s 41-6 loss to the Seahawks in the divisional round of the playoffs and was under pressure for a poor draft class from this previous year’s NFL Draft. Lynch has served as the architect of building the modern-era 49ers in 2017 and has been on a mission to capture the franchise’s sixth Super Bowl. One of the first moves he made in his role was finding the team a head coach. Lynch landed on Kyle Shanahan, who was the AP NFL Assistant Coach of the Year winner in 2016 when he was the offensive coordinator of the Atlanta Falcons, who suffered a heartbreaking loss in Super Bowl 51, when they gave up a 28-3 lead in the second half. With Lynch leading the way in the 49ers’ front office and Shanahan calling the shots on the field, the 49ers have been to two Super Bowls and four NFC Championship Games, but have yet to win the Vince Lombardi Trophy. Despite the 49ers’ failed efforts of winning the Super Bowl over the last nine years, San Francisco’s organization made a complete turnaround under Lynch’s guidance, as the team snapped a six-year playoff drought during his second season. John Lynch and Kyle Shanahan standing side by side during a team practice. AP Lynch’s front office has been responsible for drafting and developing players like George Kittle, Fred Warner, Deebo Samuel, Nick Bosa, Dre Greenlaw, Talanoa Hufanga, and their franchise quarterback, Brock Purdy — whom they selected with the final pick of the 2022 NFL Draft. Lynch has also been responsible for trading for star talent, such as Trent Williams, Jimmy Garoppolo, Emmanuel Sanders, and Christian McCaffrey. Garoppolo led the 49ers to the Super Bowl during the 2019-2020 season, while Williams became the team’s franchise left tackle for the last seven seasons. item.title: Penge birdies the 18th twice and wins RSM Classic in a 4-way playoff to keep PGA Tour card
item.description: ST SIMONS ISLAND, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 23: Marco Penge of England poses with the winner’s trophy after winning The RSM Classic 2026 at Sea Island Resort on November 23, 2026 in St Simons Island, Georgia. (Photo by Jonathan Bachman/Getty Images) Getty Images Marco Penge went from the verge of losing his PGA Tour card to winning the season finale at the RSM Classic on Monday, making birdie on the 18th hole to be part of a four-way playoff and winning on the first extra hole with a 4-foot birdie putt. Penge, who closed with a 5-under 65, was the only player to birdie the par-4 18th on the Seaside course all four times he played it, and it proved valuable in so many ways. The 28-year-old from England, who was No. 120 in the FedEx Cup coming into Sea Island, now has a two-year exemption that puts him in the Championship Series with its $20 million prize funds when it starts in 2028. Michael Thorbjornsen, already a PGA Tour winner this year at the Rocket Classic, missed a 6-foot birdie putt in regulation for the win. He shot 67. Haotong Li of China closed with a 65 and Max Greyserman shot 66 to be part of the playoff. All three missed birdie chances after Penge stuffed wedge into 4 feet on the first extra hole. “The last four, five weeks has been really tough with my game,” Penge said. “I’ve just been putting the work in and I said to my team as long as I give everything I can, the result is the result. If I lose my card and stuff like that, then it is what it is. I’m over the moon.” The result was particularly crushing for Li, who was at No. 134 in the FedEx Cup. He was projected to get his card until Thorbjornsen in the final group made birdie on the 18th to make it a four-way playoff, and then Penge wound up winning. The three-way tie for third moved Li to No. 103, just over 10 points shy of the top 100 for a full card in 2027. He thought he had his card when he headed to the playoff, and learned only after it was over that it wasn’t enough. “But everything’s done for a reason,” Li said. “I could have to go somewhere next year and play at DP (World Tour in Europe), so there’s so many consequence in life, so you’ve just got to keep up and doing what you’re doing. The result will come.” By the end of a cool, overcast and quiet Monday finish in the rain-delayed tournament, Penge was the only player to move into the top 100, bumping out David Lipsky, who missed the cut. item.title: North Carolina reportedly lands 5-star forward CJ Rosser, giving Michael Malone nation's top 2 prospects in his first recruiting cycle
item.description: The results on the court in Michael Malone's first year as North Carolina's head coach have so far been mixed. But he's crushing it on the recruiting trail. Per multiple reports i ncluding from On3's Joe Tipton , five-star forward CJ Rosser committed to North Carolina on Monday. An athletic, 6-10 forward, Rosser is a two-way player and a capable 3-point shooter. He's the No. 2 prospect in the Class of 2027, according to Rivals. North Carolina secured the commitment of No. 1 prospect DeMarcus Henry (small forward) last week, giving the Tar Heels the top two prospects in the Class of '27, per Rivals , and the nation's No. 1 ranked class as of Monday. Among others, North Carolina also has offers out to No. 4 overall prospect Beckham Black (point guard) and No. 16 overall prospect Nasir Anderson (point guard). Rosser also received offers from Kansas, Kentucky, Michigan and Louisville, among others. Michael Malone's decision to hire Chuck Martin from John Calipari and Arkansas is paying off. Ryan Hunt via Getty Images Malone hired John Calipari's recruiting coordinator Malone took over at North Carolina in the offseason to replace Hubert Davis, a UNC alumnus and former player who struggled to maintain the program's lofty standards in his five years as head coach. Malone joined North Carolina as a virtual NBA lifer and the first head coach without ties to the program since Frank McGuire took the reins in 1952. He previously coached the Denver Nuggets to eight winning seasons out of 10 and the franchise's first NBA championship in 2023. But his arrival came with questions about his ability to adjust to college basketball after spending his previous 22 seasons coaching in the NBA. He gave himself an early leg up. Malone's first staff hire was to lure Chuck Martin away from Arkansas as his associate head coach. Martin was John Calipari's recruiting coordinator at Arkansas and during his latter years at Kentucky in addition to working as an assistant under Calipari at Memphis. He also worked for Malone when Malone was the head coach at Manhattan from 1999-2000. The hiring is already paying dividends for Malone and North Carolina. On the court, the Tar Heels are off to a 4-1 start without having yet played a top 25 opponent. Their loss arrived at home to unranked Georgia on Nov. 13. They have upcoming non-conference games against Arkansas and Kentucky among others before getting into the heart of their ACC slate.

When senior quarterback Ty Dieffenbach was carted off the field after sustaining a hip injury on the first play of overtime, it appeared the fourth-ranked Bruins might have to overcome another season-altering injury at the most important position on the field. However, following a report from CBS's Pete Thamel and head coach Bob Chesney's comments Monday, the Cal Poly transfer might not miss a game after all. Dieffenbach has led UCLA to a 5-1 record since taking over under center, completing 99 passes for 1,406 yards and eight touchdowns while throwing four interceptions this season. "He's going to do everything in his power to get himself ready," Chesney said. "He's been in treatment all day Sunday and all day today." item.description: Brady Hart was able to move the ball some against Oklahoma but had just one score in his first start. (Brian Bahr/Getty Images) COLLEGE STATION - Texas A&M still has a quarterback decision to make. Days before the Aggies close their season against rival Texas at Kyle Field, Mike Elko said Monday that he had not yet decided whether Brady Hart or Marcel Reed would start at quarterback. The choice comes after Hart made his first career start Saturday in a 27-7 loss at Oklahoma , completing eight of 20 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown and one interception. The sophomore was sacked three times. "Whoever we think gives us the best chance to win," Elko said when asked what would determine the decision. As he has since 2024 when taking over for an injured Conner Weigman, Reed has handled the overwhelming majority of A&M's snaps this season, completing 160 of 287 passes for 1,712 yards, eight touchdowns and nine interceptions. Reed has also rushed for 206 yards and three touchdowns on 80 carries for a total of 1,918 yards of offense. Hart has appeared in five games during the 2026 campaign and has completed 22 of his 44 attempts for three touchdowns and three interceptions. Hart, whom Elko described Saturday as facing too much defensive pressure to ever truly get comfortable, has recorded 13 yards of negative yardage on five rushing attempts. Elko said Hart showed enough against the Sooners to reinforce one trait A&M's offense needs from its quarterback: the ability to push the ball down the field. "At his best he is able to push the ball down the field, and I think you saw that (in) the two throws that he made to Isaiah Horton, you know, giving us a chance," Elko said. "He even made one to Aaron Gregory that I thought was a good throw that I thought could have given us a chance." Hart's longest completion against Oklahoma came early in the second quarter, a 39-yard pass to Mario Craver which immediately preceded his lone touchdown pass of the day - a 36-yard reception to Horton. Elko's assessment of Hart's performance centered less on the raw numbers than on the potential for explosive plays. "If we can't push the ball down the field, it's very hard to back people off of us," Elko said. item.description: We now know what prompted argument between Larkin and Yzerman The Dylan Larkin trade request saga has been one of the most talked-about storylines in Detroit hockey circles for months now, and fans have been left guessing about what exactly went down behind closed doors. We knew something had gone sour between the Red Wings captain and general manager Steve Yzerman, but the specifics remained murky. Well, thanks to some digging by local hockey reporter Jake of 313Hockey, we're finally getting a clearer picture of the two incidents that reportedly pushed this relationship to the breaking point. The Post-Olympics Fallout According to multiple sources confirmed by the reporter, the first crack in the Larkin-Yzerman relationship came after the 2026 Winter Olympics. Larkin apparently took his sweet time getting back to the Red Wings following the conclusion of the Olympic tournament. The delay was significant enough that Yzerman himself had to personally reach out to his captain to find out where he was. The quote attributed to Yzerman is about as blunt as you'd expect from Stevie Y: "I'm paying you to be captain of the Red Wings." Now, it's worth noting that the reporter himself expressed some skepticism about the exact timeline of this particular incident. The Olympic gold medal game took place on February 22nd, and the Red Wings were back at practice by February 25th, which is a pretty tight window. Some fans recalled seeing Larkin celebrating in Miami rather than hustling back to Detroit, which, given the team's historically rough March performances in recent years, didn't exactly sit well with the fanbase. You'd think the captain of a team fighting for relevance would be eager to get back in the lineup, but apparently that wasn't the case. The Argument That Changed Everything The second and seemingly more explosive incident happened after the regular season wrapped up. Yzerman and Larkin reportedly got into a heated argument that escalated well beyond a typical end-of-season review. Things apparently got so intense that Yzerman told Larkin he was stripping him of the captaincy. Shortly after that confrontation, Larkin submitted his trade request. That sequence of events paints a pretty clear picture of how things unraveled. When your GM, a guy who is arguably the most respected captain in franchise history, tells you he's taking the "C" off your jersey, that's about as serious as it gets in hockey. And for Larkin, it seems like the response was to ask out rather than fight to earn it back. Fan reaction has been split but largely critical of Larkin. Many have pointed out that Yzerman isn't the type to hold players to standards he didn't hold himself to during his legendary playing career.
